newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-TEN-MEN JUVENTUS AND MILAN BOTH WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TEN-MEN JUVENTUS AND MILAN BOTH WIN.

text.p: Italy's European Cup representatives Milan and Juventus had stars Edgar Davids and Zinedine Zidane sent off for second yellow card offences on Sunday but both fought back to win difficult away matches 2-1.
Michele Padovano and Alessandro Del Piero scored late goals as European Cup holders Juventus recovered from the dismissal of French midfielder Zidane for their first-ever win at Perugia.

At Bologna, an 87th minute red card for Dutchman Davids failed to stop Milan bringing Bologna's 100 percent start to the season to a halt with second-half goals from Marco Simone and Liberian George Weah.

Juve join Parma and Inter at the top of serie A with seven points from three matches, although Parma, 3-2 winners over Reggiana in a match played on Saturday, lead the trio on superior goal difference.
Padovano, brought on in the second half for his first match of the season, raced 45 metres before rounding Yugoslav goalkeeper Alexandar Kocic for Juve's opener in the 84th minute.
Del Piero added a second before Marco Negri, who earlier had a goal disallowed in a controversial offside decision, scored a late consolation goal for Perugia.

In Bologna, Weah, with his third goal in three matches, rounded his marker Marco De Marchi before beating Francesco Antonioli with an angled shot in the 61st minute to clinch Milan's first away win of the season.
Earlier Russian Igor Kolyvanov's penalty had briefly equalised Marco Simone's 48th minute opener.
The win will boost the champions' morale ahead of their midweek European Cup match at Rosenborg following recent successive setbacks to Sampdoria and Porto.
Italian Cup and Supercup holders Fiorentina recovered from their poor start to the season -- one point in two matches -- with a convincing 2-0 home win over bottom-of-the-table Verona.

Zidane's afternoon started ominiously when a second minute free-kick rebounded off the post with Kocic well-beaten. Minutes later the Frenchman was booked for a late challenge and he was sent off midway through the second-half for a two-footed tackle.

But the loss of the playmaker appeared to galvanise Juventus and within minutes, Padovano had set them on the way to victory, making amends for a series of first-half misses by Alen Boksic and Nicola Amoruso.
With Bologna dominant in the first half, Milan took the lead against the run of play in the 48th minute, when Simone fired a superb volley past Antonioli.
But things looked bad when four minutes later and for the third time in successive matches, Milan's defence, badly missing the injured Franco Baresi, gave up the lead.
French interntational Marcel Desailly brought down Swede Kennet Andersson and Kolyvanov converted the spotkick.
But the 40,000 sell-out crowd had reckoned without the inspirational Weah, whose superb finish sealed Bologna's first home defeat since May 1994 when they were still playing in the third division.
Unfancied Vicenza moved into fourth spot, leading a cluster of six teams with six points on goal difference thanks to a 4-1 home victory over Atalanta.

Felippe Inzaghi gave the visitors a surprise 41st minute lead from the penalty spot, but an own-goal from Stefano Rossini and Fabio Viviani's volley turned the match in two minutes on the brink of halftime.
Cagliari's Uruguayan Fabian O'Neill scored with a first-time shot from 30 metres but was later sent off for a second bookable offence as the Sardinians went down 2-1 at home to Udinese.
Oliver Bierhoff, two goal hero of Germany's Euro 96 triumph over the Czech Republic, scored his side's winner as Udinese claimed their second successive away victory.
